Benchmark.title: ExampleOS Security Technical Implementation Guide
Benchmark.description: A demo benchmark for a fictional operating system, showing what the app produces. Rule text is written for this demo; the NIST and CCI references are public mappings.

Rule.title: ExampleOS must display a notice and consent banner before granting access.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Showing a banner before logon tells users that the system is monitored and what use is authorized. Without it, there is no record that a user was told, which weakens later enforcement.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>
Rule.rationale: Users must acknowledge the terms of use before they reach a session.

check.check-content:
Check the SSH daemon banner setting:
$ grep -i '^banner' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
If no banner is configured, or it points at a file without the approved text, this is a finding.

Rule.fixtext: Write the approved notice to /etc/issue.net, set 'Banner /etc/issue.net' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config, and restart sshd.

Rule.title: ExampleOS must not allow direct root logon over SSH.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Logging on directly as root leaves no trail of which administrator did what. Administrators should log on with their own account and elevate, so actions are attributable.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>

check.check-content:
$ grep -i '^permitrootlogin' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
If the value is not 'no', or the line is missing, this is a finding.

Rule.fixtext: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

Rule.title: ExampleOS must lock an account after three failed logons in 15 minutes.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Unlimited logon attempts let an attacker guess passwords at leisure. A lockout threshold slows brute-force attacks to the point of being impractical.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>

check.check-content:
$ grep -E 'deny|fail_interval' /etc/security/faillock.conf
If 'deny' is greater than 3 or 'fail_interval' is less than 900, this is a finding.

Rule.title: ExampleOS passwords must be at least 15 characters long.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Password length is the biggest single factor in how long a password takes to crack. Short passwords fall to offline attacks quickly.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>
Rule.rationale: Raises the cost of offline cracking.

check.check-content:
$ grep -i minlen /etc/security/pwquality.conf
If 'minlen' is less than 15 or not set, this is a finding.

Rule.title: ExampleOS audit logs must be readable only by root.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Audit records are how an intrusion gets reconstructed. If ordinary users can read or change them, an attacker can learn what is watched and cover their tracks.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>
Rule.rationale: Protects the integrity of the audit trail.

check.check-content:
$ stat -c '%a %U' /var/log/audit/audit.log
If the mode is more permissive than 0600 or the owner is not root, this is a finding.

Rule.title: ExampleOS must use FIPS-validated cryptography for remote sessions.
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>Remote sessions carry credentials and commands. Unvalidated algorithms may have weaknesses that let an attacker read or alter the session.</VulnDiscussion> <FalsePositives></FalsePositives> <FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives> <Documentable>false</Documentable> <Mitigations></Mitigations> <SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance> <PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts> <ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools> <MitigationControl></MitigationControl> <Responsibility>System Administrator</Responsibility> <IAControls></IAControls>
Rule.rationale: Confidentiality and integrity of remote administration.

check.check-content:
$ fips-mode-setup --check
If FIPS mode is not enabled, this is a finding.

Rule.fixtext:
$ fips-mode-setup --enable
Reboot for the change to take effect.
